summary: All four in-scope findings (3.2.1-3.2.4) are confirmed by code reading in core/queryalgebra/evaluation/.../optimizer/cascades/packed (PackedLogicalRuleProgram = PLRP, PackedDomainFacts, PackedQueryCodec); the reviewer's e2e evidence stands, although the workspace surefire reports have been deleted so the implementer must re-run the two repro classes to re-establish the red baseline. Two findings are binding/scope bugs with one root: PLRP treats an EXISTS subquery's dependency set as outputs(subquery) (addScalarDependencies:3620-3630) and the MINUS->NOT EXISTS rule (addCorrelatedMinusAlternative:381-421) checks only outputs(L)∩outputs(R) while both the plain FILTER NOT EXISTS alternative and the 'minus-assured-shared' anti-join execute by substituting every left binding into the body (FilterIterator:361-370 via BindingAssignerOptimizer). The design introduces one shared PLRP analysis, relationReferencedNames(expressionId) (roadmap 4.1 'referenced'), makes every planner-derived EXISTS record its full referenced-name set (existsScalar:1685-1701), uses it for liveness/dependencies, and adds a precise substitution-equivalence guard for the MINUS rewrite (fv(R)∩pv(L) ⊆ shared, no nested MINUS/INTERSECTION right side or aliasing sub-select touching a shared name, no BIND target in shared); this also answers the planner half of 3.4.4. The domain-fact findings have three independent roots: the PackedDomainFacts lattice treats 0 as 'none' for kind/language bits in widen/intersect while every seeded VALUES fact leaves them 0 = unknown (3.2.3); expandAnchorValue's finite fallback (PLRP:2748-2760) and the code/type rule (PLRP:706-755, 967-983) join by term identity for value-equality filters (3.2.4a/b); and codec deriveGroupFacts (PackedQueryCodec:383-421) derives facts from every group member so one unsound alternative narrows the whole group's facts (3.2.4c) — fixed by deriving facts only from a group's seed expression (groupId == expressionId), mirroring PackedBindingFacts' first-member policy. Each fix is independently landable and behind a precise guard rather than a rule kill switch.

findings.title: EXISTS/IN/ANY/ALL dependencies computed from subquery outputs instead of referenced names (unused-OPTIONAL pruning and projection-below-ORDER drop observed bindings)
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results: DISTINCT/COUNT/NOT EXISTS/ORDER BY EXISTS ... LIMIT; e2e-confirmed by reviewer, reports not re-run here)
findings.rootCause: PLRP.addScalarDependencies (core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/cascades/packed/PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:3607-3631) handles EXISTS/IN/COMPARE_ANY/COMPARE_ALL at :3620-3630 by calling addRelationOutputs(subquery) — i.e. only the variables the body can BIND ({s,c} for `EXISTS { ?s :r ?c FILTER(?c=?b) }`), not the variables it REFERENCES (?b lives only in the inner FILTER). The comment at :3623-3627 states the intended semantics ('an optional-bound variable that also occurs in the subquery is observed') but the code does not implement it. The codec already records the exact referenced set for parsed EXISTS in the scalar's semanticScope slot (PackedQueryCodec.java:1243-1247, nameSetPayload(VarNameCollector.process(subQuery))) and PLRP.addCommutableScalarDependencies:580-583 already consumes it — addScalarDependencies simply ignores it. Consumers that go wrong: pruneUnusedOptionals FILTER branch :3066-3071 (childLive lacks ?b) -> LEFT_JOIN branch :3119-3128 finds observedRightBindings = rightOutputs ∩ live = {} -> relationAssuresAll(left,{}) true -> OPTIONAL removed (optionalRemoved=true) -> addUnusedOptionalAlternative :2958-2989 emits the alternative for DISTINCT/REDUCED/GROUP observers; addProjectionBelowOrderAlternative :1866-1889 computes orderDependencies at :1875-1878 via addScalarDependencies -> ?b missing -> containsAll(projected={s}, deps={s}) passes -> Projection pushed below ORDER, dropping ?b before the ORDER key EXISTS reads it. Planner-derived EXISTS (existsScalar(int) :1685-1687 passes referencedNamesId = 0) never carry a referenced set at all, and IN/ANY/ALL (PackedQueryCodec.compareSubqueryScalar:1379-1385) also record 0.
findings.fix: (1) Add a shared PLRP analysis `void addRelationReferencedNames(int expressionId, long[] output)` / `long[] relationReferencedNames(int expressionId)` = all binding symbols syntactically occurring in the relation tree (over-approximation is sound for both liveness and the 3.2.1 guard): STATEMENT_PATTERN/ZERO_LENGTH_PATH/TRIPLE_REF/REIFIED/ANNOTATION -> addPayloadTerms; ARBITRARY_LENGTH_PATH -> payload terms + child; BINDING_SET_ASSIGNMENT -> name set; FILTER -> child + addScalarDependencies(condition); LEFT_JOIN -> children + condition deps; EXTENSION -> child + each element target + element scalar deps; PROJECTION/MULTI_PROJECTION -> child (all inner names, deliberately not masked by the projection) + source and target names of every element; GROUP -> child + key names + aggregate deps; ORDER -> child + order element deps; SEMI_JOIN/ANTI_JOIN -> children + condition; JOIN/UNION/DIFFERENCE/INTERSECTION/LATERAL/DISTINCT/REDUCED/SLICE/QUERY_ROOT/DESCRIBE/MATERIALIZE -> children (DIFFERENCE and LATERAL include BOTH children, unlike addRelationOutputs); TUPLE_FUNCTION -> all payload terms; SERVICE/UNSUPPORTED/default -> children plus a 'complete=false' signal (return boolean) so callers that need completeness (3.2.1) decline. Symbols exclude constant vars because PackedQueryCodec.term():1393-1406 only interns symbols for !hasValue vars, matching VarNameCollector. (2) In addScalarDependencies :3620-3630 replace addRelationOutputs(subquery) with: `int referencedNamesId = scalars.semanticScopeId(scalarId); if (referencedNamesId != 0) addNameSet(referencedNamesId, output); else addRelationReferencedNames(payloads.childGroupId(subqueryPayloadId, 0), output);` — the codec payload when present, the structural set as fail-safe fallback; never outputs-only. (3) Make every planner-created EXISTS carry a complete referenced set: change existsScalar(int subqueryId) :1685-1687 to compute nameSetPayload(relationReferencedNames(subqueryId)) instead of 0 (the 2-arg overload used by 3.2.1 passes the full set explicitly). This also completes PackedBindingFacts.deriveScalarSchedulingFacts:173-178 (scalarEmbeddedReferenceMask) for derived EXISTS, so PackedJoinEnumerator waits for every referenced outer binding before scheduling a derived NOT EXISTS. (4) Optional precision guard so the fix does not over-decline: in addProjectionBelowOrderAlternative :1875-1880, after collecting orderDependencies, `andInto(orderDependencies, relationOutputs(relations.childGroupId(orderExpressionId,0)))` before the containsAll/projectionPreservesNames checks, so EXISTS-local variables (e.g. ?c) that the ORDER input cannot bind do not block the rewrite; pruneUnusedOptionals needs no masking because `live` is only ever intersected with right outputs. (5) Record referenced names for IN/COMPARE_ANY/COMPARE_ALL too: PackedQueryCodec.compareSubqueryScalar:1379-1385 should pass nameSetPayload(VarNameCollector.process(subquery)) as semanticScopeId (keep the argument scalar as child), so the same slot convention holds for all four subquery scalars; PackedBindingFacts:173-178 only reads it for EXISTS today — extend that `if` to the four operators (behaviour-improving, cost-model only). Soundness: over-approximating dependencies can only keep more OPTIONALs and decline more pushes; it cannot introduce a wrong plan.

findings.title: MINUS -> correlated NOT EXISTS / minus-assured-shared anti-join ignores variables the MINUS body references but does not output (planner half of 3.4.4)
findings.severity: S1 (rows silently removed; reviewer confirmed e2e on LMDB with VALUES ?x + 3000 :q triples; cost-dependent)
findings.rootCause: PLRP.addCorrelatedMinusAlternative (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:381-421): sharedNames = outputs(L) ∩ outputs(R) (:384-385); the guard (:386-389) requires shared non-empty, assured on both sides and safeCorrelatedMinusProbe(R) (:604-627, an operator allow-list that admits FILTER/EXTENSION/PROJECTION/LEFT_JOIN/GROUP/DIFFERENCE bodies). Nothing checks variables that R merely REFERENCES: for `?x :p ?n MINUS { ?x :q ?m FILTER(?n = ?m) }`, outputs(R) = {x,m}, so ?n (bound by L, referenced by the inner FILTER) is invisible; the same for a nested MINUS right side (`MINUS { ?x :q ?m MINUS { ?x :r ?n } }`, outputs(R) = outputs(left child) per addRelationOutputs:3531-3534). The rule then (a) emits a plain FILTER(NOT EXISTS(R)) alternative (:393-401) whose EXISTS records only the shared names (:393), and (b) emits typed ANTI_JOIN alternatives with SEMI_ANTI_MINUS_ASSURED_SHARED (:408-415) plus the SEMANTIC_ASSURED_SHARED_MINUS_FILTER flag (:406-407) that PackedJoinEnumerator.scheduledFilterSemanticKind:7822-7841 and PackedPlanMaterializer.semiAntiJoin:252-274 turn into the 'minus-assured-shared' hint. At execution both forms evaluate R per outer row by substitution of ALL outer bindings (FilterIterator.existsProbeFunction/evaluateSubstitutedExists :353-370 -> BindingAssignerOptimizer.VarVisitor:47-53 replaces every Var whose name is bound, including ?n inside the FILTER and inside nested MINUS right sides), i.e. NOT EXISTS semantics, whereas MINUS compares only on dom(μ)∩dom(ν) and never lets ?n reach R. Additional inequivalences admitted by the allow-list even when every referenced-but-not-output var is excluded: substituting a shared var into a nested DIFFERENCE/INTERSECTION right side turns that Var into a constant so the inner compatibility domain shrinks (StatementPattern evaluation does not bind valued Vars), and an aliasing sub-select `SELECT (?y AS ?x)` captures the inner ?x. PackedQueryCodec already computes the exact referenced set for parsed EXISTS (:1243-1247) but the MINUS rule builds its EXISTS from packed relations, so it needs the structural analysis from 3.2.2.
findings.fix: In addCorrelatedMinusAlternative add a precise substitution-equivalence guard before any alternative is created, and only then emit the FILTER NOT EXISTS alternative, the typed anti-joins and the semantic flag (all three share the guard; the hint may only be attached when it passes): P1 (existing) shared = pv(L)∩pv(R) ≠ ∅ and shared ⊆ assured(L) ∩ assured(R); P2 (new, the fix for this finding) referenced(R) ∩ pv(L) ⊆ shared, where referenced(R) = relationReferencedNames(R) from 3.2.2 and the helper must report completeness (decline on SERVICE/UNSUPPORTED/unknown operators); P3 (new) no DIFFERENCE or INTERSECTION nested anywhere in R whose RIGHT child (both children for INTERSECTION) references a shared name: `intersects(shared, relationReferencedNames(rightChild))` -> decline (the substituted constant leaves the inner compatibility domain, changing which rows the inner MINUS removes); P4 (new) every PROJECTION/MULTI_PROJECTION in R is transparent for shared names: for each shared name n referenced inside the projection's body there must be an element with source == target == n (otherwise inner-scoped ?n is captured); simplest conservative implementation for this landing: decline any PROJECTION/MULTI_PROJECTION inside R carrying PackedNodeMetadataArena.VARIABLE_SCOPE_CHANGE or any element with source != target, and relax to the precise rule later; P5 (new, cheap belt-and-braces) no EXTENSION element in R targets a shared name and no GROUP in R has a shared name that is not a group key (both already implied by assured(R) via extensionAssuresSymbol:3487-3496 / groupKeyAssuresSymbol:3498-3503, so implement as an assert-style guard). Implement as `private boolean substitutionEquivalentMinusBody(int rightId, long[] shared, long[] leftOutputs)` called at :386-389 next to safeCorrelatedMinusProbe. Then: pass nameSetPayload(relationReferencedNames(R)) (not sharedNames) as the EXISTS referenced-name payload at :393 so liveness/commutation/scheduling (3.2.2 consumers, addCommutableScalarDependencies:580-583, PackedBindingFacts:173-178) see the full dependency set, while the correlation-key payload for addTypedSemiAntiAlternatives (:412) stays nameSetPayload(sharedNames) (under P2 it equals referenced(R)∩pv(L), i.e. exactly the outer bindings that influence R). Also in addSemiAntiAlternatives (:456-457) compute correlatedNames = outputs(L) ∩ referenced(R) (not ∩ outputs(R)) so LMDB's semi/anti costing (LmdbMappedSemiAntiCosting) sees the true probe-key set; correctness there is unaffected because the executor recomputes keys, but memo/hash-key cost estimates are otherwise optimistic. Answer to 'which MINUS bodies may be emitted with the minus-assured-shared hint': exactly those satisfying P1-P5 and safeCorrelatedMinusProbe; in words: bodies where every variable that the left side can bind is a shared, assured, unaliased, non-BIND, non-nested-MINUS-right variable — for those, substitution of the outer row equals selection of compatible rows and NOT EXISTS ≡ MINUS. This fix does not reverse a merge-time decision (the FilterOptimizer MINUS push-into-left decision from the merge notes is wp9's; the correlated-MINUS rule predates the merge).

findings.title: Domain-fact lattice treats 0 kind/language bits as 'none' in widen/intersect while VALUES-seeded facts leave them 0 = unknown (UNION with VALUES literal becomes EmptySet / filter wrongly dropped)
findings.severity: S1 (wrong results: langMatches(lang(?o),'*') and lang(?o)='' over UNION with VALUES; reviewer confirmed e2e on LMDB)
findings.rootCause: PackedDomainFacts.widen (core/queryalgebra/evaluation/src/main/java/org/eclipse/rdf4j/query/algebra/evaluation/optimizer/cascades/packed/PackedDomainFacts.java:181-217) computes kindBits = left|right (:189) and languageBits = left|right (:190). In this encoding 0 means 'no proof' (PackedPredicateRange.reset:65-71 zeroes everything; datatypeVerdict/kindVerdict/langMatchesVerdict in PLRP :2221-2305 all treat 0 as unknown, and widen itself treats datatypeBits 0 as unknown at :193-196 and universalBits with & at :191). VALUES facts seeded by PackedQueryCodec.seedBindingSetAssignmentFact:537-568 set STATE_KNOWN, finite values and kindBits only — languageBits stay 0 = unknown although the values include "a"@en. So for `{ VALUES ?o {"a"@en} } UNION { ?s :p ?o }` with the LMDB provider proving :p objects are LITERAL/LANGUAGE_WITHOUT/xsd:string, widenBranches (:130-143) yields kinds LITERAL, language 0|WITHOUT = WITHOUT, i.e. a proof that every union row is a language-free literal. PLRP.langMatchesVerdict:2283-2305 then returns VERDICT_ALWAYS_FALSE (:2302) -> addPredicateRangeFilterAlternatives:1937-1948 emits EmptySet (PREDICATE_RANGE_EMPTY); languageVerdict:2254-2275 returns ALWAYS_TRUE for lang(?o)='' -> filter dropped and "a"@en leaks through. intersect (:148-178) has the mirror-image defect: kind = left & right and `kind == 0 -> STATE_EMPTY` (:158-161) would prove emptiness whenever one side has unknown kinds (currently unreachable because the LMDB provider always sets kinds when domain.mask()!=0 and VALUES seeding always sets kinds — reviewer refuted it as fragile), and languageBits = left & right (:165) silently degrades a known side to unknown (imprecise, not unsound).
findings.fix: Make the lattice honour 'unknown ≠ none' (roadmap 4.3) uniformly in PackedDomainFacts: (1) widen: kindBits = (left==0 || right==0) ? 0 : left|right; languageBits = (left==0 || right==0) ? 0 : left|right (datatypes and universal already correct). (2) intersect: kinds = left==0 ? right : right==0 ? left : left&right; only when BOTH are non-zero and the AND is 0 -> STATE_EMPTY; languageBits = left==0 ? right : right==0 ? left : left&right; if both non-zero and the AND is 0, the range admits no literal: if kinds == KIND_LITERAL -> STATE_EMPTY, else clear KIND_LITERAL from kinds and set languageBits 0 (sound, keeps IRIs/bnodes). Add a private static `meetBits/joinBits` pair with a javadoc stating the convention (0 = unknown/top) and use them for kind and language. (3) Make VALUES seeding precise so the fix does not just lose all language/datatype knowledge: in PackedQueryCodec.seedBindingSetAssignmentFact:537-568 compute languageBits (LANGUAGE_WITH if any literal has a language tag, LANGUAGE_WITHOUT if any literal has none) and datatypeBits (addDatatype for each literal whose CoreDatatype is XSD; if any literal has a non-XSD datatype such as rdf:langString or a custom IRI, leave datatypeBits 0 = unknown for the whole set); leave universalBits 0 (nothing proven) and no integer bounds. Only set languageBits when kinds include KIND_LITERAL. (4) Audit the other consumers of the two bit fields for the same convention: PLRP.datatypeVerdict:2237 already guards `languageBits != 0`; expandAnchorValue:2746 requires languageBits == LANGUAGE_WITHOUT (0 correctly falls through); PackedDomainFacts.addAdmittedFiniteValue:250-253 guards kinds != 0 — no change needed, list them in the PR as verified. Soundness argument: with 0 = top the join of a known and an unknown range is unknown (may only lose precision), and the meet of a known and an unknown range is the known one; verdict rules only fire on non-zero bits.

files.change: Treat 0 as unknown for kindBits and languageBits in both lattice operations; EMPTY only when both sides are known and disjoint.
Derive languageBits and (XSD-only) datatypeBits from the VALUES literals; keep universal bits 0.

findings.title: Predicate-range anchor: finite-domain fallback expands a value-equality filter by term identity (equals) instead of SPARQL value equality
findings.severity: S1 planner-level (unit repro red per reviewer; e2e requires a finite stored domain from the LMDB provider, which LmdbPackedPredicateRangeProvider:86-90 does emit when RdfTermDomain.isFinite())
findings.rootCause: PLRP.addRangeAnchorAlternative (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:2574-2616) replaces FILTER(?o = c) by JOIN(VALUES ?o {expanded}, input) — a term-identity join — so the expansion must contain every stored term value-equal to c. expandAnchorValue (:2698-2762) handles boolean/canonical-integer/date/dateTime/xsd:string families with proofs, and for any other literal falls back at :2748-2760 to scanning the finite stored values with `stored.equals(value)` (:2753), i.e. term equality. With stored {"1"^^integer, "01"^^integer, "1.0"^^decimal, 2} and FILTER(?o = 1) the anchor is VALUES {"1"^^integer} and s2/s3 (value-equal) are lost. The same fallback is reached for VALUES-seeded finite facts (codec :537-568) — the containsBindingAssignmentFor guard at :2581 blocks the filter-input case, but not a finite fact arriving through a JOIN sibling or UNION widening. finiteRangeContainsTerm:2688-2694 (used by valuePossiblyEqualsRange for IRIs/bnodes only) is term-based by design and is correct.
findings.fix: In the finite fallback (:2748-2760) select stored values by SPARQL value equality exactly as the FILTER would: for each finite stored value v, r_strict = QueryEvaluationUtility.compare(v, constant, CompareOp.EQ, true) and r_lenient = compare(v, constant, EQ, false); include v iff both are Result._true; if one is _true and the other is not (strict-mode dependent, e.g. some string/plain-literal or timezone cases) return -1 (refuse the whole expansion, 'unsafe-lexical-equivalence') because the planner does not know the strategy's strict flag (DefaultEvaluationStrategy:1995-2013 threads `strict` per strategy); incompatibleValueExpression/_false -> excluded (the FILTER would raise a type error / be false for that row, so excluding it is equivalent); illegalArgument -> refuse (-1). Keep the existing `count == expandedCount ? -1 : count` tail (an empty selection is not a proof of emptiness under value equality unless every stored value compared to a definite _false/_incompatible; return expandedCount (0 added) in that case so the caller's `expandedCount == 0 -> EmptySet` path stays sound only when all comparisons were definite; otherwise -1). Also apply the same value-equality selection in collectStoredFiniteDomain/addStoredPredicateRangeAnchorAlternative? No — that rule anchors a pattern object on the complete stored domain without a filter, term identity is correct there. Do not touch canReplaceFilterWithFiniteAnchor/finiteDomainTermIdentitySafe (already string-only). This keeps the optimization for numeric constants when the stored domain is finite (previously wrong) and removes the c5 poisoning vector for this rule (fact {1} becomes {1, 01, 1.0}).

findings.title: Finite code/type rewrite (FINITE_CODE_TYPE_VALUES) replaces a value-equality FILTER by a term-identity VALUES join without the term-identity guard used by the finite-filter rule
findings.severity: S1 planner-level (unit repro c4CodeTypeRewriteWithoutScopeFlags red per reviewer evidence; e2e reachable on LMDB when the pipeline clears UNION scope flags)
findings.rootCause: PLRP.addFiniteCodeTypeAlternative (PackedLogicalRuleProgram.java:706-755) rewrites `{ ?e a T1 . ?e :code ?c . VALUES ?t {1 2} FILTER(?c = ?t || ?c = 3) } UNION {… T2 …}` under COUNT(DISTINCT ?e) into JOIN(JOIN(VALUES ?c {codes}, VALUES type {T1,T2}), JOIN(?e a ?type, ?e :code ?c)) (:728-742) — the FILTER is gone and ?c is matched by term identity against the code domain. analyzeCodeTypeBranch (:779-830) / collectAssignmentValues (:951-963) / appendBranchCodeValue (:967-983) collect raw value ids with only an `instanceof Value` check; no datatype/lexical guard. Stored "1.0"^^decimal value-equals the constant 1 in the original filter but not in the join, so e1 is dropped (count 1 instead of 2). The analogous finite-filter rule guards exactly this via finiteDomainTermIdentitySafe (:3254-3264, string/langString only) and canReplaceFilterWithFiniteAnchor:1921-1929; the code/type rule never calls it. PackedRewriteBindingSafetyTest#finiteTypeDomainPreservesNumericValueEquality (:94) appears to cover this but uses VF.createLiteral(1) (xsd:int) for both the codes and the stored value, so it only exercises term-equal numerics.
findings.fix: Guard the code/type rewrite with the same term-identity criterion as the finite-filter rule: after collectAssignmentValues/appendBranchCodeValue complete for both branches (or in compatibleCodeTypeBranches:832-841), require every collected code value (branchCodeValueIds[0..count)) to be an IRI, a BNode, or a Literal whose CoreDatatype is XSD.STRING or RDF.LANGSTRING (factor finiteDomainTermIdentitySafe into a static `termIdentitySafe(Value)` and reuse it in both rules). Decline the rewrite otherwise. Optional precision follow-up (not required): when the stored :code range fact is known with UNIVERSAL_CANONICAL_INTEGER and integer-family datatypes, expand numeric codes through expandIntegerAnchorValue exactly as addRangeAnchorAlternative does; without such a proof, decline. Also strengthen PackedRewriteBindingSafetyTest#finiteTypeDomainPreservesNumericValueEquality to use xsd:integer codes vs stored xsd:int/xsd:decimal so it actually tests value equality (it will then require the guard).

findings.title: Group-wide domain-fact poisoning: PackedDomainFacts.put intersects facts contributed by every alternative in a memo group, so one unsound alternative narrows the facts every sibling and every parent group consumes
findings.severity: S1 planner-level structural (repro c5 red per reviewer via addEmptyDomainJoinAlternative; symptom disappears once 3.2.4a/b are fixed but the mechanism remains)
findings.rootCause: PackedQueryCodec's fact/rule fixpoint (PackedQueryCodec.java:383-395) calls deriveGroupFacts(relationId) for EVERY relation id, including alternatives that rules appended into existing groups (PLRP.addAlternative:3179-3195 -> relations.internLogicalIfSameGroup), and deriveGroupFacts (:400-421) writes into relations.groupId(relationId). PackedDomainFacts.put (PackedDomainFacts.java:65-90) strengthens an existing fact by intersect (:69-70). So for FILTER(?o = 1) whose group gains the anchor alternative JOIN(VALUES ?o {1}, input) (3.2.4a), deriveJoinFacts (:427-462) of that alternative puts finite {1} into the FILTER group (both children assure ?o -> intersect at :439), overriding the seed's copyAll(child) fact; the enclosing JOIN with `?t :w ?o` (stored finite {1.0}) then intersects {1} ∩ {1.0} by object id (mergeFiniteValuesIntersect:229-249) -> STATE_EMPTY, and PLRP.addEmptyDomainJoinAlternative:2049-2062 emits EmptySet for the whole join (c5AnchorFactsPoisonJoinDomain). The intersection is sound only under the memo invariant that all group members are equivalent, which every rule bug violates; PackedBindingFacts already refuses to rely on that invariant (deriveRelationOutputs:236-243 and deriveRelationAssuredBindings:284-292 derive from the first member only), so the two fact systems disagree on policy. Verified that a group's id equals its seed expression id: PackedExpressionInterner.internCanonical:113-119 passes `size + 1` as the group id and alternatives are added with the target group id (internLogicalIfSameGroup:79-85), hence `relations.groupId(id) == id` identifies the seed.
findings.fix: Adopt the seed-only policy (roadmap 4.1 'computed once per memo group', 4.6 fail-safe): in PackedQueryCodec.deriveGroupFacts (:400-421) return immediately unless `relations.groupId(relationId) == relationId` (the seed), so facts are derived once per group from the original expression, and alternatives are consumers only (PLRP rules read facts of their INPUT groups: rangeVerdict/addRangeAnchorAlternative/addEmptyDomainJoinAlternative all use relations.groupId(child) or the rule's own group). Canonical relations created by rules (canonicalRelation:1025-1031, addCanonical:3168-3177) start new groups and are their own seeds, so their facts are still derived. Keep PackedDomainFacts.put's intersect for legitimate same-group re-derivation (fixpoint re-runs on the seed are idempotent) but add a javadoc stating that group facts are derived from the seed expression only. Consequence: an unsound alternative can now only mis-plan itself (still caught by 3.2.4a/b), never poison siblings or parents. Precision loss: the FILTER group no longer inherits the anchor's narrowed domain; the only consumer that benefited was rangeVerdict on a sibling FILTER over the same variable, which is exactly the c4FiniteRangeAnchorPoisonsSiblingFilterVerdict poisoning path, so nothing sound is lost. Alternative considered and rejected: keep intersection but require a 'certificate' per alternative — more machinery, same result. Also add a debug invariant (assert or PackedMemoInvariantException under a test-only flag) in PackedDomainFacts.put that an intersect never turns a non-EMPTY seed fact into STATE_EMPTY within one group, which would have flagged c5 immediately.
